summary:
Lunar Days Out is a browser game that helps children ages 7–12 explore the trade-offs of running a lunar outpost. Players guide an astronaut to collect samples, return them to the research lab, and complete research while managing suit air and battery, stamina, food, and base power. Solar panels generate power and the greenhouse uses power to grow food. NASA’s archived DONKI solar particle event times shape the scenario, while shelter choices and game risks make the consequences playable.

https://web-production-e7c1f83c.up.railway.app/
details:
Players explore a small lunar south-pole outpost and collect three samples, carrying one at a time back to the research lab. Completing research costs base power and earns a research point. The astronaut’s suit air and battery drain outside; movement also uses stamina, and low stamina or battery slows the astronaut. Meals restore stamina when eaten inside.

The solar array generates base power over time. The greenhouse uses power to grow food and can be switched off. From the control room, the player can spend power to reinforce the shelter; the greenhouse pauses while that work is underway. These choices create a simple trade-off between exploring, producing food, doing research, and preparing for a solar event.

The game replays historical NASA DONKI SEP event timestamps from January 23–31, 2012. It groups nearby records into game episodes and presents warnings as the simulated clock advances. The warning lead time, event duration, exposure meter, and gameplay consequences are simulation rules—not radiation measurements at the Moon. DONKI event records do not provide a lunar base dose reading.
dataRefs: NASA DONKI — Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) API
